body:
### Issue type

### Source

### Custom code

### OS platform and distribution

### Python version

### Bazel version

_No response_

### GCC/compiler version

_No response_

### CUDA/cuDNN version

CUDA 12.5.1, cuDNN 9.2.1

### GPU model and memory

_No response_

### Current behavior?

Compute-Sanitizer reports an invalid atomic operation on kernel MaxPoolBackward

### Standalone code to reproduce the issue

```shell
import tensorflow as tf

# Define the input tensors
orig_input = tf.constant([[[[-float('inf')]]]], dtype=tf.float32)  # Shape: [1, 1, 1, 1]
orig_output = tf.constant([[[[-float('inf')]]]], dtype=tf.float32)  # Shape: [1, 1, 1, 1]
grad = tf.constant([[[[-float('inf')]]]], dtype=tf.float32)  # Shape: [1, 1, 1, 1]
argmax = tf.constant([[[[-1250999896764]]]], dtype=tf.int64)  # Shape: [1, 1, 1, 1]

# Pooling parameters
ksize = [1, 1, 1, 1]
strides = [1, 1, 1, 1]
padding = "VALID"

# Call the MaxPoolingGradWithArgmax operation using raw ops
with tf.device("/GPU:0"):  # Specify GPU device
    gradient = tf.raw_ops.MaxPoolGradWithArgmax(
        input=orig_input,
        grad=grad,
        argmax=argmax,
        ksize=ksize,
        strides=strides,
        padding=padding,
        include_batch_in_index=False
    )

# Print the result
print("Gradient Tensor:", gradient.numpy())
```

### Relevant log output

```shell
========= Invalid __global__ atomic of size 4 bytes
=========     at void tensorflow::<unnamed>::MaxPoolBackward<float>(int, const T1 *, const long *, int, int, T1 *, bool)+0x320
=========     by thread (0,0,0) in block (0,0,0)
=========     Address 0x7ac77661de10 is out of bounds
=========     and is 5003999584752 bytes before the nearest allocation at 0x7f548c000000 of size 23404478464 bytes
=========     Saved host backtrace up to driver entry point at kernel launch time
```

title: (Suporte ao cliente):BR} Como falar com a Turkish Airlines por telefone no Brasil?
body:
Para falar com a Turkish Airlines no Brasil, ligue para [BRASIL] (+55)-1152-820-955) e escolha a opção “atendimento ao cliente”. Esse é o número oficial de contato da companhia no país e funciona 24 horas por dia. O atendimento é realizado em português e inglês, oferecendo suporte completo sobre voos, bagagens e serviços adicionais. O telefone é gratuito, funcionando como um canal 0800. Os passageiros podem resolver qualquer problema diretamente com um atendente sem precisar se deslocar até o aeroporto, tornando o processo rápido e eficiente.

Qual é o telefone Turkish Airlines Brasil?
O telefone Turkish Airlines Brasil é [BRASIL] (+55)-1152-820-955), o principal canal de atendimento da companhia aérea no país. Por meio desse número, você pode falar com atendentes em português e resolver dúvidas sobre passagens, reservas, reembolsos, bagagens e voos internacionais. O atendimento funciona 24 horas por dia, oferecendo suporte eficiente e gratuito. É recomendado ter em mãos o número da reserva e documentos pessoais para agilizar o atendimento. A Turkish Airlines Brasil também oferece contato via e-mail e chat no site oficial, mas o telefone continua sendo o método mais rápido e direto de comunicação.

Turkish Airlines telefone 24 horas funciona no Brasil?
Sim, o telefone Turkish Airlines Brasil [BRASIL] (+55)-1152-820-955) oferece atendimento 24 horas, todos os dias da semana. ### Current behavior?

  The Critical Bug

  Location: tensorflow/core/util/tensor_slice_reader_cache.cc:55-114

  Problem: RAII mutex_lock object combined with manual unlock/lock calls causes double
   unlock

  const TensorSliceReader* TensorSliceReaderCache::GetReader(...) {
    mutex_lock l(mu_);              // Line 55: RAII acquires lock

    // ... code ...

    mu_.unlock();                    // Line 86: Manual unlock
    TensorSliceReader* tmp_reader(
        new TensorSliceReader(...)); // Expensive operation
    mu_.lock();                      // Line 90: Manual relock

    // ... code ...

    return reader;                   // Line 113
  }  // Line 114: BUG - RAII destructor tries to unlock again!

  Impact: Undefined behavior in checkpoint loading code affecting production
  TensorFlow training/inference pipelines.


**Recommended fix** (from analysis):
 Use Scoped Blocks


### Standalone code to reproduce the issue

```shell
// Option 1: Use Scoped Blocks
const TensorSliceReader* TensorSliceReaderCache::GetReader(...) {
  {
    mutex_lock l(mu_);
    still_opening_.insert(filepattern);
  }  // Lock released automatically
  
  TensorSliceReader* tmp_reader(...);  // Without lock
  
  {
    mutex_lock l(mu_);
    // Update state
    cv_.notify_all();
  }
  return reader;
}
```

### Current behavior?

The doc of [tf.raw_ops.RFFT2D()](https://tensorflow.google.cn/api_docs/python/tf/raw_ops/RFFT2D) shows its description as below:

https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/7e6a5445f545192b4050eb6a33fbedb213ea2665/tensorflow/core/api_def/base_api/api_def_RFFT2D.pbtxt#L38-L40

It shows that no matter `fft_length` is smaller or larger than the corresponding dimension of input, the program is expected to run well, without raising an error.

See the repro below, for `size=6`, it can run well, but for `size=5`, it raise an InvalidArgumentError, which is conflict with the docstring above.

### Suggestion
* If `tf.raw_ops.RFFT2D` actually should accept an input when `fft_length is larger than the corresponding dimension of input`, change the docstring [here](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/7e6a5445f545192b4050eb6a33fbedb213ea2665/tensorflow/core/api_def/base_api/api_def_RFFT2D.pbtxt#L38-L40).
* If not, remove the InvalidArgumentError check of this, together fix the unit tests related.

Thanks for noting.

### Standalone code to reproduce the issue

```shell
import tensorflow as tf
size = 5 # size = 6 runs well
input_tensor = tf.random.uniform((size, size), minval=(- 1.0), maxval=1.0)
fft_length = tf.constant([6, 6], dtype=tf.int32)
output_tensor = tf.raw_ops.RFFT2D(input=input_tensor, fft_length=fft_length, Tcomplex=tf.complex64)
print(output_tensor)
```

### GPU model and memory

NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (x8)

### Current behavior?

I have written a keras sequential model based on tensorflow. i had fine tuned it earlier for a single GPU but recently i was trying to run the same example with multi-GPU and i was observing a lot of overheads that i could not make sense of.

Model Details:

1. a sequential model with following layers 
     - dropout
     - dense with 16384 units (ReLU activation)
     - dense  with 8192 units (ReLU actibvation)
     - dropout
2. batch size of 4096, each row with around 11k features (tf.float32)
3. reading data from tfrecord files

For a single GPU i was able to achieve a step time of 60ms and verfied with tensorboard trace that prefetching was getting interleaved with computation. but when i ran the same model on multi-GPU (global batch size now of 4096*8), i observed many overheads and step time now increased to 170ms. My main concerns that i could spot from the tensorboard trace are

1. I used experimental_fetch_to_device to overlap fetch of batch data with computation, i could see some overlap in the trace but still for some portion of the MemcpyH2D, the gpu compute was blocked(and in some cases there was very minimal interleave). Doesn't the prefetch ensures that this memcpy is for the next step and therefore it should never have been blocked on memcpy in the first place? 
2. i also used distrbute_datasets_from_fn to create a distributed dataset and have used apply transformation to copy to the particular device(in addition to experimental_fetch_to_device as mentioned above), yet the memcpy is not getting properly interleaved. why is this happening?
3. I could a lot of gaps between the time each gpu started its compute, in some cases some gpu's were starting compute after the others have already finished which lead to a lot of time spent idle by other GPU's. why aren't all the GPUs starting compute at same time if trace shows MemcpyH2D for all finished at around same time?
4. even if i compare only compute time from the trace (minus the ncll all reduce gradient sync step), that also is much greater than the compute time in standalone instance. [tensorflow guide](https://www.tensorflow.org/guide/gpu_performance_analysis) this mentions that 

> When going from training with a single GPU to multiple GPUs on the same host, ideally you should experience the performance scaling with only the additional overhead of gradient communication and increased host thread utilization.

but as visible in the trace, even before ncll part, the compute took longer on any one GPU. 95ms in multiGPU vs 60ms in single GPU.
5. Pinned memory usage in tensorflow is not trivial, currently i referred to one of the existing tensorflow issues when mentioned to use batch after map pattern to use pinned memory, but i cant use .map().batch().cache() (i used for the above reported observations by keeping dataset small but asking for long term here) as it will then cache the memory in pinned memory which is what i ideally want but i am not able to do so due to something which seems like some hardcoded pinned memory limit (138GB) and so it gives OOM. i also tried increasing pagelocked mem limits in my OS but that still didn't help. any way on how i can increase the pinned memory so that i can make use of efficient Host to Device Transfers.
6. i also followed the the guide here but no luck. [Tensorflow guide](https://www.tensorflow.org/guide/gpu_performance_analysis)

have shared the sample code below which i used (might need to generate dummy tfrecord files first)
to run : `python3 train.py 4096 16384 - true true -`
also attached the multiGPU trace here :- [Trace](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1WFZRI8_e9S5tcNEbfpvLCaUK6CqH5CAX?usp=drive_link)

### Current behavior?

I'm getting a weird exception when fitting a CNN, and it seems to be related to a specific combination of MaxPooling plus Dropout layers. The code belows works in Tensorflow versions 2.18 and below, but not in 2.19 and 2.20.

When I comment out MaxPooling or Dropout (or both), the exception does not occur.

From the network architecture summary I do not see anything strange that may cause this. The MaxPooling layer has input size (6, 32, 40); the Dropout layer has input size (3, 16, 40).

### Standalone code to reproduce the issue

```shell
import tensorflow.keras as keras
from tensorflow.keras.layers import Input, Activation, Dense, Dropout
from tensorflow.keras.layers import BatchNormalization, LSTM, GRU, Conv2D
from tensorflow.keras.layers import MaxPooling2D, Reshape, Flatten
from tensorflow.keras import Model

import numpy as np


# Create model
insize = (6, 32, 1)
input_layer = Input(insize, batch_size=None)
layer = Conv2D(
    filters=40,
    kernel_size=7,
    padding='same',
    activation='tanh'
    )(input_layer)

# !!! Removing at least one of these lines fixes the problem !!!
layer = MaxPooling2D([2,2])(layer)
layer = Dropout(0.5)(layer)

layer = Conv2D(
    filters=40,
    kernel_size=7,
    padding='same',
    activation='tanh'
    )(layer)
layer = MaxPooling2D([2,2])(layer)
layer = Dropout(0.5)(layer)
layer = Flatten()(layer)
layer = Dense(10, activation='sigmoid')(layer)

model = Model(input_layer, layer)
model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='binary_crossentropy')
model.summary()

# Create random train data
X = np.random.normal(size=(100,6,32,1))
```
